newsitem.title: USA: Newspaper says McVeigh admitted planting Okla. bomb.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper says McVeigh admitted planting Okla. bomb.

text.p: Oklahoma City bombing suspect Timothy McVeigh has told his defence team he bombed the Alfred P. Murrah federal building during the day to get a "body count" and send a strong message to the government, The Dallas Morning News reported on Friday.

The newspaper said in a special report published on its Internet page that it had seen defence team documents summarizing several interviews with McVeigh in which he detailed some of the preparations for the April 19, 1995, attack which killed 168 people.
The newspaper said McVeigh's lead attorney Stephen Jones would not confirm the contents of the documents but said they were either stolen or fake and should not be published.
"I don't presume to know everything everybody has said ... but none of that sounds familiar to me," The Dallas Morning News quoted Jones as saying.

But the newspaper said it obtained the documents legally and that one document detailed a 1995 interview in which McVeigh explained why he did not plant the bomb to explode at night, when the Alfred P. Murrah federal building would have been empty.

"Mr. McVeigh looked directly into my eyes and told me 'That would not have gotten the point across to the government. We needed a body count to make our point'," the defence team staff member wrote in notes of the interview, according to the newspaper.

It also said McVeigh implicated his co-defendant Terry Nichols in the bomb plot but insisted that he alone drove the explosives-filled truck that destroyed the federal building in downtown Oklahoma City.
